purpose: Add only source-supported task workflow edges. These describe a recommended order when carrying out the named task; they are not compulsory course prerequisites and never block a learner who skips or already knows an item.

approvals.condition: When deriving a population measure from a census, survey, or administrative source, first check how that source was collected, defined, and covered. This is a task workflow, not a requirement to take a separate course first.
approvals.rationale: The original declaration pointed from measures to appraisal, but the reviewed direction says source appraisal comes first. The graph encodes the corrected direction only for a task that derives measures from a selected source.

sources.title: United Nations Statistics Division, Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics
sources.locator: Principles 2, 3, and 5: professional methods, transparent source/method information, and source choice based on quality. Applied narrowly as source/context appraisal before deriving or interpreting a population measure.

sources.title: United Nations Statistics Division, National Quality Assurance Frameworks
sources.locator: National quality assurance guidance includes assessment of administrative and other data sources; supports checking source quality before using derived measures.

approvals.condition: When the chosen task uses mapped or spatially aggregated data, check the source, geographic unit, and scale before interpreting the spatial analysis. You may learn the concepts together.
approvals.rationale: This is a project workflow for interpreting spatial results, not a prerequisite for learning spatial analysis as a method.

sources.title: Office for National Statistics, Choropleth maps
sources.locator: Guidance on geographic aggregation and choosing an appropriate geographic level for a choropleth; supports checking spatial unit and scale when interpreting mapped comparisons.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
sources.locator: GIS data discussion of scale, accuracy, and lineage; supports checking provenance and scale before interpreting spatial analysis.

approvals.condition: When the selected evaluation design calls for quantitative analysis, choose an analysis that fits its question, comparison, data, and design. Skip this branch when quantitative analysis is not suitable.
approvals.rationale: Analysis choice follows from the evaluation question and design; the link is conditional on choosing a quantitative evaluation route and does not imply every evaluation needs quantitative analysis.

sources.title: HM Treasury, The Magenta Book: Central Government guidance on evaluation
sources.locator: Chapters 2 and 3: scope evaluation questions and design before selecting suitable evaluation approaches and methods; method choice must align with the question and available evidence.

approvals.condition: Before accessing, collecting, or reusing digital data for a computational question, check where it came from, whether the planned use is permitted, and what privacy or harm risks apply. This safeguard is specific to the project.
approvals.rationale: Research design must include context, permissions, and data-subject considerations before the relevant data activity. This is an operational safeguard, not a general course prerequisite.

sources.title: Association of Internet Researchers, Internet Research: Ethical Guidelines 3.0
sources.locator: Section 2.1, Initial Research Design, and the guideline's research-lifecycle framing: permissions, social context, data subjects, and risks are considered in research design and revisited as the project evolves.

approvals.condition: For a digital-text classification task, define what the text represents, which platform or records are in scope, and how the sample was selected before making classification claims. Keep a human or non-computational alternative available when classification is not suitable.
approvals.rationale: The design/scope item informs the exact text-analysis route. This is a recommended task workflow; it does not make computational analysis compulsory.

sources.title: Association of Internet Researchers, Internet Research: Ethical Guidelines 3.0
sources.locator: Sections on initial research design and AI/ML research: define the social context, data subjects, dataset accountability, and how data and models relate to the research question.

approvals.condition: When using network analysis, define what counts as a node and a relationship, and which records are included, before interpreting network measures. You may learn the design and analysis concepts together.
approvals.rationale: Network results depend on the chosen entities, ties, and source scope. This recommended workflow protects interpretation; it is not a blocker to learning the method.

sources.title: SAGE Encyclopedia of Qualitative Research Methods, Social Network Analysis
sources.locator: Defines network analysis in terms of entities/nodes and relations/ties, which must be operationalized for the selected network question.

sources.title: Association of Internet Researchers, Internet Research: Ethical Guidelines 3.0
sources.locator: Research-design and data-accountability guidance supports documenting the source and scope of digital-trace records used to define network nodes and ties.

approvals.condition: For predictive text work, define the target and the records in scope before fitting a model, then validate it on data that did not train the model. Skip prediction when the question does not call for it.
approvals.rationale: Prediction requires a defined target and an evaluation plan; the workflow prevents unsupported claims and data leakage without making machine learning a required learning route.

sources.title: Association of Internet Researchers, Internet Research: Ethical Guidelines 3.0
sources.locator: Guidance on AI/ML in internet research: make data accountability, research scope, and the social context explicit.

sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide, Common pitfalls and recommended practices
sources.locator: Section 11.2: split train/test data before preprocessing and never fit transformations on test data; supports the validation part of this task workflow.
